The pattern is symmetry about the horizontal axis, filling missing cells by mirroring, and I confirm the center row's hole stays since it mirrors onto itself. Now I want to design another example, this time a triangle symmetric about the vertical axis, pointing upward with a hole near the center and a missing cell.

I'm laying out an 11-wide grid where each row expands the triangle from a single center column outward, then removing a symmetric block of cells at one row for the hole (which stays intact) and a chunk at another row that should get restored since it breaks the mirror symmetry. I'll build a couple of these examples using color 3.
